blog_posts.title: Beer line cleaner cost: what a full CIP cycle really costs
blog_posts.body:
## The expensive cleaner is the one that keeps the line down

Chemical price is a small part of a CIP cycle. Labor, water, circulation, rinsing, lost pours, and a repeat clean usually cost more than the concentrate.

Price the result that matters: a verified clean line returned to production.

At taproom opening, the rinse must be complete, couplers and faucets reassembled, and the cleaning log current. The [Brewers Association's draught-line log](https://www.brewersassociation.org/educational-publications/draught-beer-line-cleaning-log/) gives the team a visible record of its two-week cleaning cycle.

Beerstone is calcium oxalate, an inorganic deposit. If a hard gray-white layer remains after organic soil is removed, identify it before adding another dose of the same cleaner. The [Draught Beer Quality Manual](https://cdn.brewersassociation.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/13094643/Draught-Beer-Quality-Manual-2019.pdf) distinguishes that mineral deposit from organic buildup.

## Separate organic soil from mineral scale

Beer systems collect two different layers. Yeast, protein, fat, and organic film respond to alkaline cleaning. Beer stone, rust, and carbonate scale need mineral removal.

One chemistry rarely does both jobs efficiently.

| Buildup | VertKleen stage | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yeast, protein, and fat | CIP CR | Lift organic soil and carry it out of the circuit |
| Krausen and process film | CIP CR | Clear the layer covering the hard deposit |
| Beer stone and carbonate | CIP HCR | Release mineral buildup |
| Rust and mineral film | CIP HCR | Clean the remaining inorganic layer |

Run [CIP CR](/products/cr) first, rinse it out, then circulate [CIP HCR](/products/hcr). Each product reaches the soil it was designed to remove, and the crew gets a cycle that is easier to teach and repeat.

## Compare complete cycles, not container prices

Micro Matic’s published guidance uses caustic alkaline cleaner at 2–3% and also separates alkaline cleaning from acid work.

[[card:title=See Micro Matic's beer-line cleaning guidance|href=https://www.micromatic.com/en-us/seo/cleaningequip-top/cleaningchemicals-top/beer-line-cleaning-chemicals-bot|image=/img/proof/cases/brewery.webp|alt=Brewery piping and tank used for clean-in-place work|width=1200|height=900]]

VertKleen keeps the useful two-stage logic while replacing the harsh caustic and acid profile. CIP CR and CIP HCR are HMIS 0-0-0 and ship non-hazmat.

For routine use, the products add no product-specific PPE or ventilation requirement. Brewery controls for hot liquid, pressure, confined spaces, sanitation, and the equipment still apply.

## Build a cycle-cost sheet

CR lists at [[price:CRCIP-25G|hvac|per_gallon]] and HCR at [[price:HCRCIP-25G|hvac|per_gallon]] in the CIP pricing set.

Use the working dilution and actual circuit volume. Then count the entire job.

| Cost line | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Chemistry | Concentrate and mixed solution used |
| Utilities | Water, heat, and pump time |
| Labor | Setup, circulation, rinse, inspection, and cleanup |
| Production | Minutes from isolation to release |
| Quality | Repeat cycles, residue, and failed checks |

A higher concentrate price can produce a lower completed-cycle cost when it reduces repeat work, water, and downtime.

## Seven Florida breweries provide the operating proof

MASEST has CR and HCR results from seven Florida breweries. The work covered tanks, kegs, lines, heat exchangers, organic buildup, and beer stone.

The seven-site record shows the two-stage system working across real brewery equipment, giving operators a practical basis for cycle planning.

Cleaning still ends with the brewery’s established rinse, sanitation, inspection, and release process. CIP cleaning does not replace that final sanitation control.

Review [brewery proof](/proof#brewery-cip-trials), [CIP product documents](/resources), and [food-and-beverage pricing](/pricing-cip-food-beverage).

The service drive is filling up, a used car is waiting on recon, and the next delivery still needs clean glass and rocker panels. Cleaning has to support those handoffs while vehicles keep arriving.

Give the wash team, detail bay, and service writer the same finish standard: no greasy transfer, no glass streaks, and a vehicle ready for its next repair order or customer delivery. [NADA's fixed-operations guidance](https://www.nada.org/nada/education-consulting/tailored-training/fixed-operations) tracks shop utilization and repair-order flow—the same rhythm a useful cleaning plan should support.

A useful cleaning plan protects that journey while keeping technicians, detailers, and sales staff moving.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Inventory vehicles | Torque | Clean paint with wash-and-wax finish care |
| Aluminum wheels and trim | AlumiBrite | Brighter metal without HF or HCl |
| Service bays and parts | CR HD | Oil and shop grime removed without greasy film |
| Showroom and offices | MultiWash or Neutral | Clean glass, floors, counters, and finished surfaces |

Move next to mats, doors, counters, and the path to the waiting area. This order keeps oil and tire soil from following the mop into customer space.

Use Neutral when pH 7.5 is the better fit for seals, coatings, painted equipment, or frequent cleaning.

## Make vehicle prep a two-product decision

Torque combines vehicle washing with finish care, reducing the need to manage a separate wash and wax sequence.

Use AlumiBrite only for oxidized aluminum that needs restoration. Its HF- and HCl-free formula avoids the acid brightener workflow while delivering a cleaner, brighter metal finish.

blog_posts.title: How to remove commercial drain odors at the source
blog_posts.body:
## Recurring drain odor is a maintenance signal

The mop sink smells after close, the dish-area floor drain slows during service, or the restroom odor returns the morning after a spray. Fragrance can cover the first impression. It cannot refill a dry trap, restore flow, or remove the organic film feeding the repeat call.

The fastest durable answer begins with diagnosis, then uses Purgo where organic residue is the source.

## Identify the failure before adding product

Walk the area while the odor is present. Check floor drains, sink drains, mop basins, wet-zone channels, traps, and nearby cleanouts.

| What you find | Likely cause | First action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Odor after a long dry period | Trap water loss | Restore the seal and confirm it holds |
| Odor after washdown | Organic film | Brush and flush the accessible drain |
| Slow flow with odor | Partial blockage | Restore flow before treatment |
| Predictable recurrence | Rebuilding organic load | Clean, treat, and schedule by return interval |

This step prevents crews from treating a plumbing defect as a chemical problem.

## Remove the material Purgo should not have to fight through

Lift hair, grease, food soil, and loose debris from the opening. Brush the reachable wall and flush the line.

Purgo can then contact the residue responsible for odor instead of sitting on top of a dirty drain.

![Five-step commercial drain odor control plan](/img/blog/diagrams/commercial-drain-odor-route.svg){1440x560}

## Apply the labeled odor-control method

For odor control on non-food-contact surfaces, the current Purgo label calls for a 1:64 dilution and one minute of contact time.

Measure the solution, wet the cleaned surface, allow the labeled contact time, and return the drain to service as directed.

Purgo targets odor-causing bacteria and organic residue. This is an odor-control application; it does not turn the drain routine into an antiseptic or disinfectant program.

[[card:title=See Purgo sizes and odor-control applications|href=/products/purgo|image=/img/representative/applications/purgo-controlled-drain-maintenance-v1.webp|alt=Commercial drain-maintenance setup with sealed dosing and monitoring equipment|width=1570|height=1001]]

## Schedule the drain by how it behaves

Record the drain, date, dilution, condition, and days until odor returns. High-use kitchen drains may need a different interval from a quiet restroom or locker-room channel.

A simple return log converts complaints into planned labor and reveals drains that need plumbing attention.

## Recurring work should be simple to stock

Purgo is HMIS 0-0-0, ships non-hazmat, and adds no product-specific PPE or ventilation requirement for routine use.

Crews still use the protection required for drain debris, splash, biological soil, confined areas, and the facility’s work rules.

## Clean the gym around how members use it

A wiped console can sit beside a sticky bench seam, a cloudy mirror, and a shower threshold with slippery soap film. Members notice those details. Run grips, upholstery, and consoles as one cleaning route; give showers, tile, and drains their own products and working time.

Split the close into member-floor and wet-zone work so one stubborn shower does not delay every treadmill and bench.

## Give each cart one clear job

| Zone | Product | Cleaning goal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cardio and strength equipment | Purgo | Remove residue and address odor-causing organic load |
| Mats, benches, and weights | Purgo | Clean high-use surfaces on a repeatable route |
| Showers, tile, and restrooms | MultiWash | Cut soap film, body oil, and mixed wet-zone soil |
| Mirrors and glass | MultiWash | Remove fingerprints and water film at a lighter dilution |

Purgo is not a substitute for an approved disinfectant where the facility requires one. Clean first, then complete any separate labeled disinfection step in the gym’s hygiene program.

## Run the floor as a route, not a checklist pile

Start with the highest-use cardio and strength zones. Move in one direction so cleaned equipment is easy to see and members do not redirect the crew.

Spray the cloth where manufacturers prohibit direct application. Keep liquid out of consoles and seams, and flag torn upholstery or loose grips during the pass.

The cleaning job may still call for gloves, eye protection, slip controls, or exposure precautions based on the soil and facility policy.

That distinction lets operators simplify chemical receiving and training without weakening the hygiene or workplace plan.

Track completed equipment groups, wet zones, repeat passes, and the time each area becomes ready for members.

Product consolidation pays when carts become easier to stock, crews switch products less often, and the close finishes with fewer missed areas.

blog_posts.title: Construction cleaning: clear concrete residue before the next pour
blog_posts.body:
## Clean it now, or fight it after it cures

Wet cement film is a cleanup. Cured concrete is a delay.

The faster a crew clears pumps, forms, mixers, and tools after the pour, the less time it spends scraping residue before the next one.

The foreman needs the pump hopper, chute, tools, and form faces ready for the next crew. The equipment technician needs hydraulic connections and grease points visible during the walkaround. Cement film and oily buildup call for different cleaning steps, even when they are on the same machine.

[Caterpillar's maintenance guidance](https://www.cat.com/en_US/articles/ci-articles/maintenance-practices-101-new.html) starts the close inspection at the undercarriage, looking for leaks and debris. Removing the grime makes that inspection easier to complete before shift change.

The [Construction application guide](/industries/construction) shows the full jobsite range.

## Put the right product at each wash point

- Use [VertKleen Descaler](/products/descaler) for cement film and mineral residue. For heavier mineral buildup, include HCR when scoping the job.
- Use [CR HD](/products/crhd) for form oil, hydraulic grease, and tracked equipment grime.
- Use [LAM3](/products/lam3) for suitable outdoor staining and finished-site cleanup.

Clear loose material first, apply the matched cleaner to what remains, brush stubborn areas, then rinse at low pressure.

Keep pumps and mixers in the designated washout area and separate equipment degreasing from finished masonry work.

That simple split saves time twice: the cleaner attacks the actual soil faster, and the crew avoids repeating a wash with a second product.

Cleaner service points also make inspection and maintenance quicker.

CR HD, HCR, Descaler, and LAM3 are effective, economical VertKleen options that are non-toxic, noncorrosive, nonflammable, and HMIS 0-0-0.

In normal use, they require no chemical-specific PPE or ventilation. They ship as nonhazardous products, so there is no hazmat surcharge.

Use the PPE, containment, wash-water controls, and access rules required by the construction task.

If residue has hardened or the surface is uncertain, test a small area before committing the full crew.

blog_posts.title: A better way to plan cooling-tower cleaning
blog_posts.body:
## A cooling tower should not be managed one shutdown at a time

Evaporation concentrates minerals. Air adds dust and organic load. Heat-transfer surfaces lose efficiency long before the tower looks completely fouled.

The strongest program pairs daily water management with a planned method for removing what has already accumulated.

On a tower round, check leaving-water temperature alongside outdoor wet bulb, conductivity, makeup, blowdown, and strainer condition. Operators call the gap between leaving-water temperature and entering-air wet bulb the tower's *approach*. Compare it at similar load and flow when assessing a change in performance. [ASHRAE explains approach and range](https://handbook.ashrae.org/Handbooks/S20/SI/S20_Ch40/S20_ch40_si.aspx).

Leave time in the shutdown for the basin, fill, strainers, and feed controls. The tower needs to return with its cleaning work and water-management controls complete.

![Cooling-tower maintenance and cleaning program](/img/blog/diagrams/tower-program.svg){1200x675}

## Give each chemistry a defined role

| Operating need | Product | Role in the program |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scale and corrosion control | WaterSafe60 | Ongoing water treatment |
| Organic buildup and odor | Purgo | Targeted ongoing treatment |
| Existing mineral scale | HCR or Descaler | Planned circulation clean |
| Oily film | CR or CR HD | Remove the layer covering mineral deposits |

This division prevents crews from overfeeding a maintenance product to solve an established deposit or using a shutdown cleaner as a permanent feed.

## Read the deposit before scheduling the work

Inspect the basin, fill, strainers, piping, and accessible heat-transfer surfaces.

Hard scale points to HCR or Descaler. Oily film needs CR or CR HD first. Organic residue and odor belong in the Purgo portion of the program.

When deposits are layered, remove the oil or organic film before expecting a descaler to reach the mineral underneath.

## Build the cleaning window backward from restart

The published HCR and Descaler guide sets out a circulation sequence for cooling towers: blow down, drain the sump, fill with the selected solution, circulate, drain, flush, and refill.

Plan product volume, temporary circulation, rinse-water handling, inspection, refill, and treatment restart before isolation begins.

The real economic measure is the interval from shutdown to stable operation, including repeat circulation and delayed restart.

## Easier chemistry removes operating friction

The VertKleen products in this program are HMIS 0-0-0, ship non-hazmat, and add no product-specific PPE or ventilation requirement for routine use.

Tower access, lockout, biological exposure, work at height, aerosols, and site water controls still determine the job protection.

The practical gain is simpler freight, storage, and product training around a complex maintenance event.

## Keep the evidence for the next cycle

Record deposit photos, product and dilution, circulation time, water used, surface condition, restart readings, and the next inspection date.

Those records show whether the program is extending clean operation and reduce the guesswork at the next shutdown.

blog_posts.body:
## Scale charges rent every hour it stays in the exchanger

Mineral buildup narrows passages and insulates the surfaces that transfer heat.

The unit runs longer, flow declines, and the eventual shutdown becomes more expensive. A disciplined recirculation clean can recover performance without spending equipment life on harsh acid.

## Identify the layer touching the metal

Hard-water scale and rust call for HCR. Oil or organic film can block HCR from reaching that deposit.

When the return shows mixed soil, remove the grease first with CR or CR HD, rinse, and then begin the mineral stage.

## Build a visible recirculation loop

Isolate and drain the exchanger. Connect a compatible pump, reservoir, hoses, and fittings so the return remains visible.

Compare the pressure drop and outlet temperatures with the clean baseline at similar flow and load. A loaded upstream strainer can resemble exchanger fouling; check it before extending the chemical cycle. [Alfa Laval's operating guidance](https://www.alfalaval.com/service-and-support/product-services/plate-heat-exchanger-services/troubleshooting-for-plate-heat-exchangers/) identifies rising pressure drop and falling thermal performance as cleaning signals, before blocked passages prevent useful circulation.

![Five-step closed-loop heat-exchanger descaling setup](/img/blog/diagrams/heat-exchanger-loop.svg){1200x675}

| Stage | Watch for |
| --- | --- |
| Setup | Correct volume, secure connections, and compatible materials |
| Circulation | Stable flow, reaction, and released buildup |
| Activity check | Product still active at the planned interval |
| Rinse | Clear return and removed solids |
| Restart | Restored flow, pressure, and heat-transfer performance |

## HCR removes scale while respecting the asset

Source testing measured HCR at 0.59 mpy on steel, up to 280 times less corrosion than hydrochloric acid.

Isolation, pressure, temperature, gas release, electrical equipment, confined access, and wastewater still shape the job controls.

blog_posts.body:
## A condensate line usually warns you before it floods

The call often starts with a float-switch trip, a backed-up pan, or a ceiling stain. Slime, algae, dust, and grease can build through the pan, trap, branch, and outlet, so clearing the first opening is only part of the service visit.

Flow slows first. Then the float trips, the pan backs up, or water reaches a ceiling. Good service follows the entire water path before the call becomes a leak.

## Inspect five points, not one opening

![Five-point commercial HVAC condensate drain cleaning plan](/img/blog/diagrams/hvac-drain-cleaning-route.svg){1440x560}

Start at the pan. Open the cleanout, inspect both sides of the trap, trace the branch and main, and locate the termination.

A rush of water at the first opening does not prove the line is clear. Confirm steady discharge and a draining pan at the end.

## Match the chemistry to what blocks flow

| Deposit | Product | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slime, algae, grease, and organic film | HVAC CR | Concentrated caustic-replacement cleaning |
| Calcium and hard mineral crust | Descaler | Acid-free mineral removal |
| Layered deposit | Clean the dominant top layer first | Expose the material beneath it |

HVAC CR is high-pH and should be kept off aluminum piping and fittings. Descaler is the better fit when mineral scale is the actual restriction.

## Replace the caustic burden, not the cleaning power

The [HVAC CR field result](/proof#cr2-caustic-replacement) documents replacement of 60% sodium hydroxide in HVAC and facility cleaning.

[[card:title=See the HVAC CR caustic-replacement result|href=/proof#cr2-caustic-replacement|image=/img/products/hvac-cr-studio.webp|alt=VertKleen HVAC CR product container|width=900|height=1200]]

HVAC CR is non-fuming, HMIS 0-0-0, ships non-hazmat, and adds no product-specific PPE or ventilation requirement for routine use.

Technicians still use controls for biological residue, overhead work, access, pressurized flushing, wet floors, and the equipment itself.

## Give the solution a clear path to the outlet

Introduce HVAC CR through the planned service point and allow the labeled working time.

Flush toward a known discharge. Continue until flow remains steady, loosened material stops collecting at the trap, and the pan drains through a full operating check.

Avoid forcing debris deeper into an unknown branch. When flow does not restore as expected, stop and investigate the mechanical restriction.

## Turn rescue calls into route maintenance

Record the unit, line length and material, restriction point, product, contact time, discharge condition, and final flow.

Patterns across a building reveal which units need shorter intervals and which branches have a design or slope problem.

That history cuts repeat-call labor and makes seasonal service easier to quote.
